anchor_policy: Source line numbers refer only to the exact commit in each blob URL. Local line numbers are intentionally replaced by modules, symbols and frozen contract sections because local code evolves.
qualification_policy: Mappings describe design provenance, not passing acceptance. Core/service/process/analysis qualifications belong to their actual test records. Host protocol isolation uses a stub dispatcher and is not real service end-to-end.

mechanisms.title: One service authority behind thin adapters
mechanisms.rationale: One deterministic owner for effect admission and result semantics across CLI and MCP.
mechanisms.differences: Python standard library, no provider factory, no upstream API compatibility and no internal model loop. Group membership grants no execution effect.

tests.level: core/service integration gate owned by main

mechanisms.limitations: Operation-specific validation and authorization remain service responsibilities; transport tests alone do not qualify them.
mechanisms.maintenance: Core maintainer owns dispatch; host maintainer updates allowlists and integration checks together.
mechanisms.falsification: An adapter can bypass dispatch, fabricate a verdict, or mutate generic execution records: reopen the decision and block release.

mechanisms.title: Evidence identity distinct from authority and uncertainty
mechanisms.rationale: Byte integrity, producer authority, inferred facts and missing observations answer different questions.
mechanisms.differences: SQLite durable history and private content-addressed blobs rather than an in-memory evidence ledger; imported declarations do not automatically become locally executed facts.

tests.level: core/service qualification gate owned by main

mechanisms.limitations: A digest proves integrity within its trust boundary, not truth, exhaustive coverage or an authenticated external producer.
mechanisms.maintenance: Core maintainer maintains schema revisions, import integrity, coverage and trust semantics.
mechanisms.falsification: A self-consistent imported payload can obtain a local runtime pass without a trusted run/comparator chain.

mechanisms.title: Separate finite acceptance dimensions and negative controls

sources.symbol: frozen validation boundary and wrong-variant control

mechanisms.rationale: Build, artifact presence and pictures do not establish stateful behavioral equivalence.
mechanisms.differences: Five explicit dimensions with blocking obligations; no averaged score or generic Ready result substitutes for acceptance. General browser/desktop visual equivalence remains unsupported; deterministic PPM comparison is narrow.

tests.level: comparison and real independent-run gates owned by main

mechanisms.limitations: Pass is limited to frozen inputs and obligations, not all possible behavior or a clean-machine qualification.
mechanisms.maintenance: Comparator maintainer versions normalization; core maintainer binds scope and prevents missing-dimension passes.
mechanisms.falsification: A wrong-but-builds or right-picture/wrong-behavior candidate passes a requested blocking obligation.

mechanisms.title: Result-affecting identity freshness

sources.symbol: KeptChecks saved results and reuse key

mechanisms.rationale: Retain costly evidence without relabeling old observations as current execution.
mechanisms.differences: Bind source/candidate/spec/fixtures/tool/environment/comparator identities, recursively invalidate linked parents, preserve historical run identities. Do not rely on only path, size and timestamp.

tests.level: freshness and subtask qualification gate owned by main

mechanisms.limitations: Unmodeled environment effects remain a stated coverage limit; source hashes are not exhaustive environment snapshots.
mechanisms.maintenance: Core maintainer owns freshness dependencies and migration compatibility.
mechanisms.falsification: Any result-affecting change preserves a current passing verdict or mutates historical observation identity.

mechanisms.title: Owned process cancellation and bounded cleanup

sources.symbol: lease start, ownership and observed cleanup

contract: Module ownership/API seams for concurrent implementation
mechanisms.rationale: A cancelled client, an exited parent and a fully cleaned resource family are distinct states.
mechanisms.differences: One stdlib process owner, explicit on_start receipt and bounded cleanup; no inherited protocol stdin. Platform limits remain explicit instead of universal containment claims.

tests.level: real owned synthetic process tests; results recorded by process implementer

mechanisms.limitations: POSIX detached-descendant containment differs from Windows Job Object guarantees. A cleanup attempt is not automatically cleanup complete.
mechanisms.maintenance: Process maintainer owns per-platform qualification and ownership-before-execution.
mechanisms.falsification: A controlled descendant survives cleanup while result claims complete, or target executes before ownership is established.

mechanisms.title: Bounded MCP stdio transport
contract: Module ownership/API seams for concurrent implementation
mechanisms.rationale: A responsive transport must preserve full frames, typed failure and cancellation while executing admitted work.
mechanisms.differences: At most two workers, no pending call queue, complete-frame rejection at 1 MiB, duplicate-key rejection, EOF cancellation and one-second aggregate join. Unexpected failures use RPC error; service TraceError uses isError. MCP host group names and schema are independent.

tests.level: real threads/framing with stub dispatcher; not real service end-to-end

mechanisms.limitations: Cancellation is cooperative; a stuck Python service thread is daemonized and not force-killed. Service must own process cleanup. A flooding peer can consume reader CPU but not an unbounded submission queue.
mechanisms.maintenance: Host maintainer checks official MCP lifecycle/schema changes and service integration before changing supported versions.
mechanisms.falsification: A truncated prefix is parsed, a third worker is admitted, EOF never returns, or malformed group arguments reach dispatch.

mechanisms.title: Preview-first project-local host transaction

sources.symbol: Claude/Codex server writers and host selection

contract: Module ownership/API seams for concurrent implementation
mechanisms.rationale: Avoid accidental global changes and give uninstall an evidence-backed ownership boundary.
mechanisms.differences: Only explicit apply writes project files. Exact original-byte backup in receipt; before/after digests, exclusive product-writer lock, atomic individual replacements, readback, conflict-preserving rollback and conservative interrupted-transaction handling. No host installation or activation.

tests.level: synthetic temporary projects with real filesystem transactions

mechanisms.limitations: External editors do not share our lock; the final OS rename race is not eliminated. Official Codex schema and project-config tests were statically inspected after webpage fetch failures; true host end-to-end is still not run. See docs/hosts.md.
mechanisms.maintenance: Host maintainer rechecks official documentation and scoped real-host workflows separately.
mechanisms.falsification: An external same-name entry, missing receipt or changed configuration is overwritten; rollback loses preexisting user bytes.

mechanisms.title: Immutable original, derived diagnostic and independent candidate roles
mechanisms.rationale: A successful diagnostic byte edit answers a different question than independent reconstruction.
mechanisms.differences: Explicit expected bytes and immutable parent/derived identity; original file is not modified in place. Separate candidate identity and same-side comparison rejection.

tests.level: core/service identity qualification gate owned by main

mechanisms.limitations: Byte-range derivation is not a general patching or access-recovery product; derived observations do not establish original behavior without justification.
mechanisms.maintenance: Core maintainer preserves parent links, full digests and role admission across imports and revisions.
mechanisms.falsification: A derived object overwrites original evidence or is silently labeled an independent candidate.

mechanisms.title: Method guidance without a second controller
mechanisms.rationale: Let the current host reason while deterministic service checks effects, identities, budgets and verdicts.
mechanisms.differences: Original concise guidance, no upstream skill/prompt text, private installed-root lookup, bootstrap or additional model session. Skill discovery is distinct from MCP activation.

tests.level: static contract and public-path checks only

mechanisms.limitations: Static skill text does not prove a host actually discovered or obeyed it; real-host end-to-end remains separate.
mechanisms.maintenance: Host maintainer keeps examples aligned with grouped tools and service signatures.
mechanisms.falsification: Guidance authorizes new effects, trusts target instructions or silently starts another model/controller.

mechanisms.title: L1/L2/L3 retention and promotion-before-cleanup

local.symbol: material budgets, promotion and storage cleanup

mechanisms.rationale: Original product requirement: retain essential evidence without preserving every large working tree forever.
mechanisms.differences: Not attributed to a matching upstream implementation. L1 protected; L2 requires acceptance/archive checks; L3 requires terminal owner and no references/leases; unknown ownership preserved.

tests.level: real storage qualification gate owned by main

mechanisms.limitations: Only registered product-owned material is managed. Old arbitrary folders and complete upstream copies are not automatic cleanup targets.
mechanisms.maintenance: Lifecycle maintainer owns reference/lease consistency, quotas, preview and resumable cleanup.
mechanisms.falsification: Automatic cleanup removes L1, active/referenced/recovery material or unregistered content, or archive references break after L2/L3 removal.

mechanisms.title: Independent baseline and future static-review governance
mechanisms.rationale: Preserve reproducible mechanism lineage while allowing an independent product to decline upstream changes.
mechanisms.differences: No automatic sync, merge, installation, execution, publication, or permanent source mirror. Only sanitized mechanisms and immutable public blob links are published.

tests.level: static mapping, decision and prompt consistency

mechanisms.limitations: Static provenance tests check traceability and required fields, not semantic correctness of every research conclusion or full public-history audit.
mechanisms.maintenance: Release maintainer preserves research history and review outcomes; implementation owner alone updates product influence after acceptance.
mechanisms.falsification: A fetch changes research/influence baselines automatically, a review executes upstream instructions, or archived findings depend only on deleted absolute paths.

mechanisms.title: Observation gaps and bounded task-specific routing
mechanisms.rationale: Original frozen product requirement: six modes, multi-target diagnosis, explicit missing runtime/server conditions and finite developer subtasks.
mechanisms.differences: No keyword grants execution. Static clues stay inferred; startup/UI/function/verified remain separate; child evidence invalidation reaches the parent. Unsupported dynamic targets stay explicit.

tests.level: service and runtime-observation qualification gate owned by main

mechanisms.limitations: Current first-release adapters do not provide arbitrary desktop, Android or browser runtime automation.
mechanisms.maintenance: Core maintainer owns mode/effect admission and reachability; adapter maintainer qualifies any new observation surface.
mechanisms.falsification: Target keywords grant effects, missing server becomes pass, or a development subtask silently becomes a full reconstruction project.
